related_questions.question: What are the downsides of mental health courts?
related_questions.snippet: The cons of mental health court are forced treatment and/or medication, lack of treatment services available, longer sentences, and the requirement of pleading guilty, which is when an offender admits to a crime whether or not they actually committed it.

related_questions.question: Do mental health courts handle both felony and misdemeanor offenders?
related_questions.snippet: Mental health courts accept individuals charged with a wide variety of offenses and may focus on individuals charged with misdemeanor crimes, felonies, or both.

related_questions.question: Can your mental health be used against you in court?
related_questions.snippet: If you have a mental health condition, the court might ask for pre-sentence and medical reports before they sentence you. These reports can help the court decide on the right sentence.
related_questions.title: Criminal courts and mental health - Rethink Mental Illness

related_questions.question: What happens when you complete mental health court?
related_questions.snippet: Participants who successfully complete (graduate) the program may have their charges dismissed (diversion), sentences reduced, or judgements vacated. They are engaged in treatment and connected to services that allow them to remain in the community.
